mainText: This is Dose of Good for Thursday, November 5. Here are 5 good news stories. First: HIV-prevention shot gets a US$40-a-year generic version. The FDA gave preliminary approval to the first generic lenacapavir, made by India's Dr. Reddy's. The original costs US$28,218 a year; the generic is meant for 120 low- and middle-income countries. Second: Therapy dogs visit patients at a hospital in Fortaleza. The Sexteto 4 Patas group brought comfort to patients at the Leonardo da Vinci State Hospital. One of them was Francisca Fábia Lopes, 51, who had been in hospital for 14 days. Third: Public school students build a necklace that calls for help to protect women. Four students at CEEPTIC in Lauro de Freitas created the Calisto necklace: two presses of its button send an alert with real-time location. The prototype cost about R$80. Fourth: 96-year-old teacher publishes her first book of 100+ handwritten poems. Ema Vargas presents "Eu Venho Oferecer Meu Coração" at the 72nd Porto Alegre Book Fair, which runs until November 15. Fifth: Chocolate made from cocoa grown in England helps future-proof the crop. A University of Reading student made six bars from greenhouse-grown cocoa. The university's centre holds more than 300 types of cocoa plant. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
